newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-NEUMANN LEADS U.S. WOMEN'S OPEN AS SORENSTAM SLIPS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NEUMANN LEADS U.S. WOMEN'S OPEN AS SORENSTAM SLIPS.

text.p: A Swede led after the first round of the U.S. Women's Open, but it was not two-time defending champion Annika Sorenstam, as Liselotte Neumann took charge Thursday on the Pumpkin Ridge course.

Sorenstam, the hot pre-championship favourite, was upstaged by compatriot Neumann, who compiled four birdies in a flawless four-under-par 67 in cool afternoon conditions following intermittent rain earlier in the day.
Neumann, the 1988 Open champion, was the only player in the 150-woman field not to make a bogey or worse as she matched her lowest round ever in a U.S. Open.
She led by one stroke over Americans Susie Redman, Kelly Robbins and Deb Richard, and 19-year-old South Korean Se Ri Pak.
Redman was helped by the first hole-in-one of her career, which came at the 15th, where her six-iron bounced three times and jumped into the cup.
Sorenstam found no such joy in her round as she shot six-over 77 in a dreadful start to her quest to win the event an unprecedented three consecutive years.
"I just had a bad day," said Sorenstam, who took triple-bogey at the ninth hole after burying a stray shot into some heavy hay. "But I never give up."
Neumann won three times on the LPGA Tour last year but languishes 51st on this year's money list.

"It's been a struggle, even though I've been working hard to prepare for this week," Neumann, 31, said. "I was a little nervous this morning but I made an incredible (par) save on number three, where I got up-and-down from 70 yards. That made me a little more comfortable.
"I started hitting the ball pretty good and overall my putting was great. I'm extremely happy with the score.
"If you're going to win the Open, you need everything to go your way, and you need a good putting week. It always seems to come down to putting."
All four of Neumann's birdies came from beyond 10 feet, including a 40-footer at the par-3 10th.
Another big name player to struggle in the first round was Briton Laura Davies, the 1987 champion.
Davies, who opened a big gash in her left index finger while slicing some bread Tuesday morning, shot a 75 to stand eight strokes off the pace.
Among those tied for second place, Robbins has the best credentials, after winning last week's Jamie Farr Classic with an all-time LPGA record low score.
She made just one bogey Thursday, at the 15th hole, which ended an incredible streak of 76 successive holes without a dropped shot, stretching back to the first round last week.
"It didn't really faze me," the easy-going Robbins said of her bogey. "You know it's going to happen every once in a while.
"I've been playing so well, hitting the ball close and giving myself a lot of opportunites. I'm kind of riding this train out."
